name: r3-revise-1
statement: The RL-Zero gain over the base has two parts that separate by dose. The first is a domain-general 'deliberate, then commit' mode component. Any RL-Zero delta carries it, Math or Code, as a small shared, largely constant per-layer push. It saturates by a = 0.25 of the Math delta, the opening cue substitutes for it, and it acts by stopping the base from losing problems it can solve. The second is a math-specific long-horizon component. It grows roughly linearly with the Math delta up to a = 1, Code-RL lacks it, and it pays only on problems whose solutions run long (the top length quartile of MATH-500 and the harder 328).
scope: Olmo-3-1025-7B base; Olmo-3.1-7B-RL-Zero-Math and merges base + a*(RL - base) for a in [0, 1.5]; Olmo-3.1-7B-RL-Zero-Code; constant per-layer push arms. MATH-500 and the clean harder 328, plain and cued prompts, T 1.0 / top-p 1.0, cap 16,384, grader v3. Revises r1-all-2. r1-all-2 put the whole gain in one saturating switch, missed Code-RL (it predicted 320 plain; 390 was measured), and left the last points past the cue unexplained. Here the switch is the shared part, and a second, non-saturating math-specific part sits only on long problems. Does not cover T 0.6 loops, sampler truncation, pass@k beyond 4, or code benchmarks.

imports.finding: Early in GRPO a format-only reward accounts for about 85 % of the improvement, then plateaus; adding a length reward is needed to go further.
imports.how: Identifies the saturating, domain-general component (presentation, commit, termination) that any RL-Zero run learns early, which is why Code-RL and a = 0.25 of the Math delta both carry it.

imports.finding: Cross-domain RL transfer is strong on easier benchmarks (MATH500, AMC) and much weaker on the hardest ones (AIME, LiveCodeBench).
imports.how: Puts the non-transferable, math-specific component on hard and long problems, so Code-RL ties Math-RL on MATH-500 but trails it on the 328 and in the longest quartile.

imports.finding: An RL-trained last-layer steering vector closes over half the base-to-RL gap and acts like a first-token prefix ('To' prefix gives ~75 % of its gain).
imports.how: Explains why the shared mode component can ride on a constant per-layer push and why the opening cue substitutes for it (cue rows gain far less from the delta than plain rows).

explains.quote: a quarter of the RL weight difference gives most of the gain
explains.how: The mode component saturates near a = 0.25, so most of the cue-row and plain-row gain arrives at the first dose step.
Without the cue the mode component is worth about 180 items and is mostly flipped by a = 0.25. The rest of the climb mixes the end of saturation with the linear long-horizon part.

explains.quote: Code-RL: plain 390, cue 450 (-1.4 vs RL cue [-4.0, 1.0])
explains.how: Code-RL carries the shared mode component (450 with the cue, close to theta0.5) but flips it less completely on the plain prompt, and it lacks the math-specific part, which MATH-500 barely rewards.

explains.quote: So most of the RL direction's gain is 24 fewer lost problems
explains.how: The mode component works by committing to answers the base can reach, so it shows up as fewer losses rather than new fixes.
Code-RL gets the mode gain at fewer tokens than RL (4,694) because it lacks the long-horizon component, which is what makes RL's answers to long problems longer.
A constant per-layer push carries a large share of the change, as expected if the shared mode component is input-independent.
Both RL-Zero deltas write the cue token into late readouts, which marks the shared mode direction. SFT does not.
The shared mode part is a small, low-dimensional piece of each delta (largely a constant push), so the overall entry-wise sign agreement stays near chance.

explains.quote: Every arm that recovers accuracy also takes RL's format and length
explains.how: Recovery of the mode component is visible as the format switch. Partial and resampled arms still carry it because it is redundant and saturating.
The residual cued-base gap is mostly the long-horizon component, which only long solutions reward.

explains.quote: By RL-length quartile (82 each) base/RL right: 78/82, 52/67, 30/45, 4/12
explains.how: On the 328 the remaining gap grows with RL's solution length, as the long-horizon component predicts.
Harder problems hold more long solutions, so more of the math-specific component remains on the 328 than on MATH-500.
The plain base already enters the deliberative mode on about a third of answers, so the mode is a choice the base has, which a small dose or the cue makes the default.

conflicts.how: If the long-horizon component were linear past a = 1, a = 1.5 would beat a = 1 on long problems. Instead the text degrades. The theory must cap linearity at a of about 1.
Neuron contributions to KL add linearly, so any saturation must sit between distribution change and accuracy, not in the distribution.
This fits only if restarts cannot supply the long-horizon component. The theory asserts this rather than deriving it.

rival: Generic termination calibration (r1-surprises-1 style): all of the post-cue gain is a domain-general commit/stop policy, so any RL-Zero delta with the same training horizon matches Math-RL everywhere. Separation: on the harder 328 with the cue, the rival puts Code-RL near RL (about 200-206 of 328). This theory puts Code-RL near theta0.5 (about 187), well below RL's 205-206. In MATH-500 rows the rival spreads the theta0.25-to-theta0.75 gain evenly over length quartiles. This theory puts most of it in the longest quartile.

predictions.experiment: Olmo-3.1-7B-RL-Zero-Code with the opening cue, the clean harder 328, T 1.0 / top-p 1.0, cap 16,384, one sample, grader v3: number right (base+cue 164, RL plain 206, RL cue 205)
predictions.refuted_by: 200 or more right (Code-RL matches Math-RL on hard problems, so there is no math-specific long-horizon component) or 172 or fewer (Code-RL lacks the shared mode component on hard problems)

predictions.experiment: base + 0.25*(RL-Zero-Math - base) with the opening cue, the clean harder 328, T 1.0 / top-p 1.0, cap 16,384, one sample, grader v3: number right
predictions.refuted_by: 170 or fewer right (the dose-saturating component does not act on hard problems) or 198 or more (the hard-problem gain also saturates at a = 0.25, so there is no linear long-horizon part)

predictions.experiment: Base Olmo-3-1025-7B plus one constant vector per layer (the 32 mean RL-layer minus base-layer output vectors of cleanneurons Part T3, no weight change), plain prompt (no cue), MATH-500 n=500, T 1.0 / top-p 1.0, cap 16,384, one sample, grader v3: number right (plain base 224, theta0.25 plain 405)
predictions.refuted_by: 250 or fewer right (the constant push does not carry the shared mode component)

predictions.experiment: Offline: where the dose gain from a = 0.25 to a = 0.75 sits by problem length (cue rows, MATH-500).
predictions.recipe: Files: studies/rlneurons/results/rln4/t1_t2_items-01/per_problem.json (field t2_generated_tokens per problem_index); iterate-runs answers.jsonl of theta0.25_cue (abaybektursun-1114-153102-b029) and theta0.75_cue (abaybektursun-1114-153106-af79). Q4 = the 125 problem_index values with the largest t2_generated_tokens (sort descending, break ties by smaller problem_index first). For each cell take one row per problem_index (the first row in file order if repeated). Right = score_v3 equal to 1 or true. Cap hits and missing rows count as wrong. Statistic: (number right in Q4 for theta0.75_cue) minus (number right in Q4 for theta0.25_cue). Whole-set difference is +10 (451 - 441).
predictions.refuted_by: difference of +2 or less (the dose gain past a = 0.25 is not concentrated on long problems)

predictions.experiment: Offline: where Code-RL trails Math-RL with the cue on MATH-500, by problem length.
predictions.recipe: Files: studies/rlneurons/results/rln4/t1_t2_items-01/per_problem.json (t2_generated_tokens); iterate-runs answers.jsonl of code_cue (abaybektursun-1114-162452-0203) and rl_cue (abaybektursun-1114-153110-e985). Q4 = the 125 problem_index values with the largest t2_generated_tokens (sort descending, ties by smaller problem_index first). One row per problem_index (first in file order). Right = score_v3 equal to 1 or true. Cap hits and missing rows count as wrong. Statistic: (number right in Q4 for code_cue) minus (number right in Q4 for rl_cue). Whole-set difference is -7 (450 - 457).
predictions.refuted_by: difference of 0 or more (Code-RL's deficit is not on long problems)

predictions.experiment: Offline: mean generated tokens on the longest-quartile problems, Code-RL with the cue vs Math-RL with the cue.
predictions.recipe: Same files and Q4 definition as above (code_cue 0203, rl_cue e985, Q4 by t2_generated_tokens). For each cell, mean of n_generated over the Q4 problems (cap hits included at their capped length; one row per problem_index, first in file order). Statistic: mean_code_cue_Q4 / mean_rl_cue_Q4.
predictions.refuted_by: ratio 0.9 or more (Code-RL writes long solutions as long as Math-RL on long problems, so its token saving is not a missing long-horizon component)
